newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crendell jumps on entertainment prospects.
newsitem.headline: Crendell jumps on entertainment prospects.

text.p: Shares in cash shell Crendell Investment Corp Ltd, whose listing was reinstated on Monday as part of a plan to create a listed entertainment firm, jumped in heavy trade on upbeat prospects for the new group, dealers said.
By 1125 GMT, Crendell shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange had added 188 cents to 310, a 154.10 percent gain -- off a best level of 320 cents -- after over 1.4 million shares changed hands.

"People are backing the characters (in the new group). There's quite a bit of experience there," one dealer said referring to some of the leading businessmen who have come together to form Sasani Investments Ltd.
These include Eric Ellerine, chairman of furniture retailer Ellerine Holdings Ltd and Welcome Msomi of black empowerment firm Msomi Ventures.
Sasani will be reverse listed into the Crendell cash shell later in December.
Traders said shares' sharp upward move was also helped by the low numbers of shares in circulation.
"There is a shortage of stock. In the rights issue which they plan to hold there is nearly 12 times more capital than in the company itself at the moment," a trader said.
Dealers said shares, which were being snapped up mainly by speculators, were looking toppish at current levels.
"It is running a bit optimistic at the moment. Dealing is very thin at these top levels," a trader said.

Sasani's owners comprise two consortiums. One consists of film company Interleisure Ltd and video firm Video Lab Group which will together hold a 41.5 percent stake. The other, also holding 41.5 percent, consists of Msomi Ventures, an investment house and an advertising consortium.
The public will hold the remaining 17 percent.
The core of its business will be video business, Video Lab, which it will buy from joint owners Interleisure and Video Lab management for 90.5 million rand paid for in cash and a share issue.
Sasani intends to raise the cash through a rights issue of 51 million rand. It plans to use Video Lab as a platform for expansion locally and offshore.
